chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
O slaves of desires, cut them short, for he who leans on the world gets nothing out of it except the pain of hardships.
ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of leaning on the world according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this concise maxim from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) employs the metaphor of the 'creaking of teeth' (sarif al-aniab) to vividly illustrate the inevitable decay and suffering that accompany aging, serving as a stark warning against excessive attachment to the transient world. This reflection aligns with the Shia scholarly emphasis on *zuhd* (asceticism) not as mere renunciation, but as a disciplined focus on the eternal, reminding believers that the physical deterioration of the body is the primary tangible cost of worldly preoccupation.
